According to the latest issue of the *Power On* newsletter, Apple is said to have once considered adding a feature to its "Apple Upgrade" programme that would make the transition to a new iPhone almost seamless: users' data would be transferred before the new device shipped. However, the feature never actually came to fruition.

The concept was simple: if users are upgrading their devices through a regular monthly instalment plan, why not make the handover as convenient as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported:

There are some obvious loopholes here. First of all, your iCloud backup would be slightly out of date, because the data can only be transferred at the moment of shipment, which is a few days after the order is placed — unless you pick up the device in person at the store.

On top of that, there are obvious privacy concerns. That said, if you've been using iCloud backup all along, it's hardly surprising that Apple has your data. But the average user might worry about how that data is transferred to the new phone and whether anyone has accessed it during the process.

Two years ago, Apple rolled out a brand-new system across its retail stores called "Presto", which allows staff to update software on an iPhone while it is still in the box. It's hard not to imagine that in the future this system could be extended to support iCloud backup transfers in which no one touches your data throughout the entire process.

However, the feature never made it to market — and that might actually be a good thing.
